Be part of that change and join our community.Our reports Manufacturing and Value Chains...Decarbonizing Manufacturing and Supply Chains for Growth: Guide for C-suite ExecutivesAmid geopolitical fragmentation, persistent economic headwinds and policy uncertainty, manufacturers and supply chain leaders are operating with tight margins and increasingly complex global footprints. As climate ambition collides with short-term performance pressures, the debate has sharpened: Is decarbonization a competitive advantage or a financial and operational burden? This white paper reframes decarbonization as a value-creation strategy – one that can strengthen operational efficiency and supply chain resilience, reduce exposure to volatility and unlock new revenue through product engineering and business-model innovation. The action needed is to move beyond compliance-driven sustainability efforts towards integrated transformation, aligning operations, finance, procurement, technology and commercial strategy around a clear business case for decarbonization. Drawing on insights from consultations with over 50 industry leaders, academic experts and innovators working across 13 industrial sectors, the paper sets out an executive-level approach to strengthen the business case for industrial decarbonization, anchored in three interconnected outcomes: bottom-line gains, business continuity and resilience, and top-line growth. Supported by real-world case studies of decarbonization solutions, the report aims to help manufacturing executives navigate implementation complexity and translate ambition into actionable strategies with measurable outcomes.26 October 2026Manufacturing and Value Chains...Mediterranean Foresight: Shaping Europe’s Future Value ChainsAs global value chains are being reshaped by geopolitical realignment, technological change and the energy transition, the Mediterranean is uniquely positioned to become a strategic corridor for Europe’s future value chains, strengthening the region’s industrial resilience and competitiveness. The paper provides governments, businesses and international organizations with a practical agenda to move from shared diagnosis to coordinated action, helping position the Mediterranean as a more connected, resilient and competitive production, energy and innovation corridor supporting Europe’s next generation of value chains.21 September 2026Manufacturing and Value Chains...Human Machine Collaboration in Industrial Operations: Activation PlaybookFully autonomous production lines already operate in automotive, electronics and semiconductor facilities around the world. Advanced robotics, machine learning and intelligent control systems are doing the work that humans performed manually five years ago. The technology is here. What most organizations lack is a clear plan for how their workforce will be ready and that gap is limiting their ability to capture value at scale.23 June 2026Manufacturing and Value Chains...Intelligent Infrastructure: A PrimerInfrastructure is in transition. No longer is it about how well a country builds and connects physical assets, but how intelligently those assets can sense, communicate, learn and act. Intelligent infrastructure is more than a technology investment – it is a determinant of national competitiveness. The aim of this report is to help policy-makers and business leaders steer this transformation in a structural system-wide way rather than as an isolated technology shift.
Intelligent infrastructure is the ability to embed system-level intelligence and autonomy into the systems that power economies. It spans industrial production, energy systems, urban services, supply chains and national security. As such, it requires coordinated action across policy, investment and governance.
This report, developed with global leaders, presents the DNA+ framework – a practical architecture comprising Devices, Network, Artificial intelligence + cyber resilience – to make the concept of intelligent infrastructure concrete. Grounded in real-world experience from expert communities including advanced manufacturing, energy and materials, cybersecurity and urban transformation, the framework maps intelligent infrastructure across four levels: Company, Cluster, City and Country. And it offers deployment pathways to translate potential into systemic value. Intelligent infrastructure is not a destination but an evolving capability: one whose strategic value will compound over time.
11 May 2026Manufacturing and Value Chains...Intelligent Industrial Operations Outlook 2026The first edition of the Intelligent Industrial Operations Outlook explores how industrial operations are shifting from traditional automation to intelligent, connected and increasingly autonomous systems. It shows how frontier technologies such as AI, physical AI and quantum technologies are transforming industrial operations, reshaping how organizations plan, produce, move and improve.
Companies are moving beyond isolated pilots towards operating models in which humans and intelligent systems work together in real time. This report maps that shift across the industrial value chain and highlights common pathways through which operations evolve from assisted intelligence to more adaptive, self-orchestrating systems.
More than a snapshot of frontier technologies, this first edition provides a practical outlook for leaders. It helps decision-makers understand where new capabilities are creating value, how operational functions may evolve across the NOW–NEAR–NEXT horizon, and which governance, workforce and investment choices will matter most in building resilient, adaptive and sustainable operations.
